article_title: THE GREAT EXHIBITION. THE OPENING OF THE GREAT EXHIBITION.
article_text: THE GREAT EXHIBITION. THE OPENING OF THE GREAT EXHIBITION. Her Majesty has consented that the state opening of the Exhibition on the Ist of May shall take place in manner corresponding with the popular character of the occasion. All who purchased season tickets will admitted. It is calculated that the ceremony of inauguration can witnessed by 15,000 people, ami that will probably be the limit to which the privilege will Ikj confined. For the concession thus made to the wishes of the people the public have in a great measure to thank Lord Granville and the Executive Committee, who duly and urgently, yet respectfully, represented the unpopularity of a state opening from which even exhibitors, after all their efforts and sacrifices, would have been excluded. the arrangement at present contemplated, her Majesty will open the building at ten o’clock, proceeding from Hyde Park-corner along Rotten-row, and entering at the eastern end, while the admission for siwctators entitled be present will be at the south end of the transept. cannot omit this opportunity of pointing out the reasons which had very nearly deprived the public of all share in a ceremonial to which they had looked forward with feelings of very natural and excusable curiosity. Whenever the Queen appears in public, people, who, from their appearance and manners, ought to know better, flock around and almost mob her. Nor is it the male sex alone, but ladies also are found guilty of this impertinence ; and it has been ascertained by experience that the policeman’s truncheon, effective it is in a street row, or under ordinary circumstances, is powerless against the wearer of a satin dress or any other form of feminine finery. Ordinary assemblages of common-place people can be kept in order; but crowds of gentlefolk, it said, cannot; and it was this difficulty that Lord Granville and the Executive Committee hud to combat in their happily successful efforts to impart to the promised pageant popular character. —The Time*. consequence of the misapprehension that has existed respecting the Queen’s visit in state on the opening day of the Great Exhibition in Hyde Park, we have made inquiries, and are enabled to state that her Majesty’s gracious consent to inaugurate the opening of the Exhibition her presence will not have the effect of excluding any single person, who was previously considered to entitled to admission to the interior of the building. The holders of season tickets will certainly be admitted, according to the terms upon which they have purchased their right; and we have further the satisfaction to add, that it probable the right of admission will Ikj extended exhibitors, who will value the privilege all the more for the advantage and pleasure of being allowed to join in the universal tribute of affection to our beloved Sovereign and her illustrious Consort, to whom this great and beneficial experiment is so largely indebted.—
